attempts.reasoning: Three gaps in the original code. (1) withConnection only calls scope.close() on the success path, so a throwing fn leaks the connection. I wrapped fn in try/catch: on throw, close the scope (releasing the connection), swallow any cleanup error, and rethrow the original error. On success, close runs and any cleanup error propagates. Because acquire() happens before the scope and release callback exist, a failed acquire releases nothing. (2) Scope.close() ran callbacks FIFO, so the connection release could happen before cursors were closed. It now runs them in LIFO order by splicing and reversing the list. (3) Scope.close() stopped at the first throw, ran callbacks a second time on repeat calls, and had no error aggregation. It now runs every callback, collects errors in throw order, rethrows a single error or throws an AggregateError for several, and returns immediately on any call after the first. Pool.release is unchanged, so double-release still throws and remains detectable. Requirements checked against the final code: release exactly once on return and on throw (the release callback is the first registered, so it runs last, and close() is idempotent); LIFO order; run all callbacks; single error vs AggregateError; second close is a no-op; original fn error wins over cleanup errors; cleanup error propagates on success; nothing released if acquire fails; double release still throws.
